[Rating: 1/10] Should you ever have the misfortune of this game landing before you, be sure to throw it into the volcano from whence it came. This actually might be the worst game I've ever played that I still *technically* classify as a game. Full of stupid placement rules and random luck (oh, you drew a tile that lets you toss out 4 huts this round because of the tile type while I got screwed again? Fun! Oh, I can't actually do the block I've been waiting for because the volcano smoke spews the same way? Neat!) Want to try to plan ahead? Might as well forget about doing that. Few games have pissed me off a

[Rating: 2/10] Another masterpiece by my favourite designer Marcel-André Casasola Merkle. But maybe there's hope. Taluva is actually slightly better game than Attika. Two points well deserved, I didn't find the game broken. And trust me – I tried.

[Rating: 2/10] Not my kind of game.  A themeless, luckless abstract strategy game with nothing to recommend it.  I just wanted my one play to be over as soon as possible.

[Rating: 2/10] I don’t get the hype for Taluva. It probably did the “place pieces on a shared board” thing well for its time but now there are so many more interesting similar games, why come back to it? Also not friendly for new players since you can easily screw over others a great deal

[Rating: 2.5/10] 2 plays with 2 players.  I felt that the experience was brain burning and dry and not in a good way. Despite the beautiful tiles, the game is a pure abstract.  Not to mention that the game has analysis paralysis and kingmaking issues.  If you are in the market for a FUN tile laying game check out Carcassonne and its many variations.

[Rating: 3/10] When I win a game, I like to feel like it was because I had a good strategy, I was really lucky, or a combination of both.  In my first game of TALUVA, I won and I had absolutely no grasp of strategy, placement tactics, and I was hazy on one or two of the critical rules.  Talk about unsatisfying.  TALUVA is a reasonable abstract game without a lick of theme despite a handsome production that plays sort of like JAVA stripped of A LOT of fat and without those stupid, pointless festivals. [Rating: 3/10] I dislike games where the key is to get the person playing before you to give you an opportunity.

[Rating: 3/10] Very very dry and very not my type of game. I'd trade it away except that Scott really likes it.

[Rating: 3/10] Dry, dull and abstract. The game is colorful - even beautiful - but that's about all it has going for it. Players are prone to over-analysis and the game plods along at a terrible pace.

[Rating: 3/10] Lovely components, but otherwise this is landfill euro. The game intrigued me but I still coudn't unpack the core mechanics in to a strategy. It's also a very dry, deterministic game. Gave away to friends.

[Rating: 3/10] This gets another hearty "meh" from me. Cool artwork and puzzly, abstract fiddling does not make a good game and certainly does not create any immersion or interest for more than a nanosecond or two.  Also, why are they building temples and towers on an island that's about to explode? Location, location, location, as they say. Or used to, before they were covered in boiling lava.

[Rating: 3/10] Blah tile laying game.  The ending was very anticlimactic and unsatisfying even though I won.
